Using \(f(2-x)=f(x)\) with \(x\) replaced by \(-x\) gives
\[
f(-x)=f(x+2).
\]
Substitute this into \(f(-x-2)=-f(x)\):
\[
f(x+4)=-f(x).
\]
Thus \(f(x+8)=f(x)\), so \(f\) has period \(8\).

Therefore
\[
f(194)=f(194-8\cdot 24)=f(2).
\]
Using \(f(2-x)=f(x)\) at \(x=0\):
\[
f(2)=f(0)=e^0=1.
\]

\[
\boxed{1}
\]
